name: gcReopens
title: GC deletes the slot below the checkpoint; the writer, still unresolved there, re-creates it: committed and acked below the checkpoint, never ingested
instance: gcReopens (GC_KEEP = false; writer faults on; TTL 3)
timing: model time is in ticks; a worker's fence = sent + TTL - MARGIN - BUDGET, its statement lands by fence + BUDGET + SLACK, another worker may take the lane at sent + TTL + MARGIN (MARGIN = BUDGET = 1 tick)

steps.action: no answer in time: slot 0 is unresolved
the exporter gives up on request 2; the queue's next call brings request 1 to the same slot (create-only, not sent yet)
the late PUT of request 2 lands (its answer goes nowhere)
check (absent) and send INSERT S1 over e1/0
verify, CAS the checkpoint past e1/0
FATAL: delete ingested data slots below the checkpoint, including e1/0 just below it (no PUT for it in flight)
send request 1 to e1/0; If-None-Match succeeds on the deleted key; S3 commits it and answers 200 (the queue acks request 1)

violated.expression: every Data ever committed is in central, or at/after an open epoch's checkpoint

design.guard: GC_KEEP: gc deletes data slots s < next - 1 only; the slot just below the position stays until the epoch retires
design.effect: step 9 deletes nothing (gcReopensDesignTest: slot e1/0 still holds payload 2); in step 10 the writer gets 412, HEADs e1/0, sees another batch, and appends request 1 at e1/1, which the consumer ingests
design.code: D12 (2026-09-26): GC keeps each epoch's slot below the position until the epoch retires (one object per open epoch)

dropped: the writer's final 200/ack step (the violation needs only the commit); the PUT's send and apply are merged in steps 1 and 10; check and send are merged in step 6
